claims.text: Real-time closed-loop monitoring with adaptive laser-power modulation will improve the dimensional precision of LPBF high-entropy-alloy components.
Real-time closed-loop monitoring with adaptive laser-power modulation will improve the mechanical integrity of LPBF high-entropy-alloy components.
Real-time closed-loop monitoring with adaptive laser-power modulation will reduce fabrication-induced defects in LPBF high-entropy-alloy components.
High-entropy-alloy components produced by standard additive manufacturing exhibit fabrication-induced defects.
High-entropy-alloy components produced by standard additive manufacturing exhibit significant dimensional inaccuracies.
High-entropy-alloy components produced by standard additive manufacturing exhibit suboptimal mechanical performance.
The proposed system can respond in real time to in situ melt-pool signatures by adjusting laser power.
Adaptive laser-power modulation can precisely control melt-pool size and cooling rate.
Typical high-entropy-alloy LPBF operates at rapid solidification rates and high thermal gradients.
Controlled melt-pool dynamics will produce more uniform solidification.
Controlled melt-pool dynamics will minimize porosity across deposited layers.
Controlled melt-pool dynamics will reduce residual stresses across deposited layers.
Adaptive laser-power control will minimize hot cracking.
Stabilizing melt-pool size and cooling rate will prevent thermal distortions and thereby enhance geometric precision.
The adaptive process will increase component strength relative to a fixed-power process.
The adaptive process will increase component ductility relative to a fixed-power process.
Fixed-power additive-manufacturing processes produce variable melt-pool dynamics.
Fixed-power additive-manufacturing processes cause greater defect formation than the proposed adaptive process.
Laser power and related process parameters affect defect formation, microstructure, and mechanical performance in additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
